title: T8: Verify release acceptance criteria and feature completion
description:
Purpose: final completion gate for the feature (closes before the epic). Design §19.1 (items 1–4), §13, §2 goals.

Checklist to verify and record:
1. Validation gates pass on a clean checkout of the working tree: restore, Release build, full tests on net8.0–net11.0, coverage ≥ 80%, mkdocs build.
2. Golden templates: existing four constructs zero diff vs the T0 baseline; new construct goldens present.
3. Workload compatibility: Next.js, ASP.NET Core shim, Blazor Static SSR synthesize via the same public API; no workload-specific construct/helper/packaging in src/.
4. Sandbox gate bead closed with full evidence (incl. Blazor page + asset).
5. Scope audit against the design: no EncryptionKey, no FromAsset, no upstream L2/alpha dependency, no changes to existing constructs' source, explicit AuthType everywhere,
   GrantInvoke matches §10.2 rev 3 (no AddToPrincipalOrResource/AssertSuccess), single resource policy, docs complete.
6. Optional spike bead (T4a) status recorded but does not block.
Outcome: notes summarizing readiness for the maintainer. Do NOT publish NuGet packages, bump versions, commit, push, open PRs, or close GitHub issue #98 — those require separate maintainer authorization.
acceptance_criteria:
- All six checklist items verified with evidence recorded in notes.
- Any gap results in a linked bug bead and this bead stays open.
- No publishing/commit/PR actions taken.

title: T5: Add Web Function testing helpers, consumer example and workload synthesis tests
description:
Purpose: consumer-facing Testing helpers plus consumer/workload compilation and synthesis tests. Design §8.6, §9 (all examples), §15 (Consumer helpers, Workloads), §19.1 item 2.

Deliverables:
- src/LayeredCraft.Cdk.Constructs/Testing/WebFunctionConstructAssertions.cs: extension methods on Template per §8.6 (ShouldHaveWebFunction, ShouldHaveRevision, ShouldHaveRevisionCode,
  ShouldHaveEndpoint, ShouldHaveEndpointScaling, ShouldHaveInvokeGrant, ShouldHaveSingleResourcePolicy, ShouldHaveNoResourcePolicy, ShouldAllowCloudFront,
  ShouldAllowResourcePolicyPrincipal, ShouldHaveWebFunctionOac, ShouldHaveCodeBucketReadStatement). Match by function/endpoint NAMES (resolve the endpoint's logical ID
  from its EndpointName), never by logical-ID prefixes; must distinguish multiple endpoints. Follow existing *ConstructAssertions style.
- src/LayeredCraft.Cdk.Constructs/Testing/WebFunctionConstructPropsBuilder.cs per §8.6 (private fields; WithFunctionName, WithCode, WithTestArtifact(Construct scope, key),
  WithIamAuthEndpoint, WithApplicationManagedEndpoint, WithEndpoint(IWebFunctionEndpointOptions), WithEnvironmentVariable, WithEntryPoint, WithTimeout,
  WithMaxConcurrencyPerEnvironment, WithRole, WithLogs; Build() throws InvalidOperationException without Code or endpoint; no Action<> callbacks; never chooses an AuthType).
- CdkTestHelper.CreateWebFunctionPropsBuilder() (additive change to CdkTestHelper only).
- Internal test kit: WebFunctionConstructAutoData attribute + customization (deterministic names) following existing TestKit patterns.
- Consumer example tests: compile and synthesize §9.1–§9.7 verbatim-equivalent code using only the public API.
- Workload synthesis tests (acceptance criterion §19.1 item 2): Next.js, ASP.NET Core (execve shim), Blazor Static SSR — each via the same public API, differences only in
  Code, EntryPoint, EnvironmentVariables, and consumer CloudFront behaviors.

Tests: assertion helpers have positive and negative tests (failing assertions throw); builder tests (Build() throws without auth/code; WithTestArtifact synthesizes without credentials).
Exclusions: new production behavior in constructs (if a gap is found, record a blocker rather than changing construct semantics); docs.
acceptance_criteria:
- Assertions and builder exist with the §8.6 signatures; CdkTestHelper entry added without changing existing helper behavior.
- §9 examples and three workload configurations compile and synthesize in tests.
- Assertions distinguish multiple endpoints and verify exactly-one resource policy.
- Coverage threshold (80%) maintained; existing goldens unchanged; validation gates pass.

title: T4: Implement WebFunctionOrigin with OAC and automatic same-stack permissions
description:
Purpose: CloudFront origin factory with OAC and automatic, same-stack permission granting. Design §5.4, §8.5, §9.4, §9.7, §11.1 (AUTHORITATIVE steps), §11.2 (spike results), §12.3, §14, §15 (CloudFront/OAC).

Deliverables (src/LayeredCraft.Cdk.Constructs/WebFunctionOrigin.cs + internal origin class):
- public static class WebFunctionOrigin:
  * WithOriginAccessControl(IWebFunctionEndpoint, WebFunctionOriginWithOacProps? = null): throws immediately for ApplicationManaged endpoints.
  * WithoutOriginAccessControl(IWebFunctionEndpoint, WebFunctionOriginProps? = null): throws for IamAuth endpoints; returns an HTTPS HttpOrigin.
- internal sealed class WebFunctionOacOrigin : DeputyBase, IOrigin (jsii interface implemented from .NET; proven by spike) whose Bind(scope, options):
  1. Signing: HomeRegion/PerRegion → Signing.SIGV4_ALWAYS_AMZ_AUTH; MultiRegion → new Signing(SigningProtocol.SIGV4A, SigningBehavior.ALWAYS_AMZ_AUTH).
  2. OAC: use supplied IOriginAccessControl unchanged (not inspected), else create one L2 FunctionUrlOriginAccessControl with child id "WebFunctionOac" in the bind scope. No CfnOriginAccessControl.
  3. Permissions Automatic: imported endpoint → throw; Stack.Of(scope) != Stack.Of(endpoint) → throw with the same-stack/dependency-cycle message and ExternallyManaged remedy;
     else endpoint.GrantCloudFrontInvoke(Stack.Of(scope).FormatArn({Service="cloudfront", Region="", Resource="distribution", ResourceName=options.DistributionId})).
     ExternallyManaged: no statement; Annotations info naming the distribution that must be allowed.
  4. Return new HttpOrigin(endpoint.DomainName, {mapped WebFunctionOriginProps members, ProtocolPolicy=HTTPS_ONLY, OriginAccessControlId=oac id}).Bind(scope, options).
- No opt-in Region list, no distribution behavior inspection, no IValidation (design §11.1 "Removed in revision 2").

Tests: OAC lambda/always-amz-auth/sigv4 for HomeRegion & PerRegion, sigv4a for MultiRegion; origin DomainName = endpoint DomainName, https-only, OriginAccessControlId set;
every WebFunctionOriginProps member passes through; auto statement aws:SourceArn = distribution ARN; same origin on two behaviors → one statement and one OAC;
two distributions → two scoped statements; origin for a second endpoint → statement on that endpoint ARN; supplied OAC reused (none created); ExternallyManaged → no statement + annotation;
explicit GrantCloudFrontInvoke(literal ARN) without a Distribution; negatives: ApplicationManaged+OAC, IamAuth+WithoutOriginAccessControl, imported+Automatic, cross-stack+Automatic
(assert the library's error message, not a CDK DependencyCycle). Golden template: Next.js-style distribution (§9.4) with default + /_next/static/* behaviors on one origin.

Exclusions: Distribution/certificate/DNS creation by the library; behavior helpers; Testing helpers; docs.
Security: OAC only for IamAuth; never forward-compatible "convenience" that would let an ApplicationManaged endpoint appear protected.
acceptance_criteria:
- WebFunctionOrigin public API matches §8.5; Bind behavior matches §11.1 steps 1–5.
- Uses L2 FunctionUrlOriginAccessControl with correct Signing; no L1 OAC, no custom resources.
- Automatic permissions only for owned endpoints in the same stack; imported/cross-stack fail with library messages; ExternallyManaged annotated.
- All listed tests pass; new golden template added; existing goldens unchanged; validation gates pass.

title: T3b: Implement GrantInvoke (revision-3 account rules) and endpoint imports
description:
Purpose: GrantInvoke with the revision-3 account-establishment rules, and limited endpoint imports. Design §8.4 (IWebFunctionEndpoint, FromEndpointAttributes, ownership semantics), §10.1, §10.2 (AUTHORITATIVE algorithm + table), §14, §15 (IAM matrix).

CRITICAL: implement §10.2 revision 3 exactly. Do NOT use Grant.AddToPrincipalOrResource and do NOT rely on Grant.Success/AssertSuccess
(verified CDK pitfall: success only checks that a statement object exists). Compose Grant.AddToPrincipal / Grant.AddStatementToResourcePolicy, check StatementAdded yourself,
and return Grant.Combine of statements actually written.

Deliverables:
- IWebFunctionEndpoint : IResource with EndpointName, EndpointArn, DomainName, Url, AuthType, EndpointType, GrantInvoke(IGrantable), GrantInvoke(IGrantable, WebFunctionInvokeGrantOptions), GrantCloudFrontInvoke(string).
  WebFunctionEndpointConstruct implements it.
- GrantInvoke algorithm (§10.2): throw for ApplicationManaged; identity side ONLY when the account is established:
  E1 = grant principal is an owned construct (Resource.IsOwnedResource) whose stack account is not literally different from the endpoint stack's;
  E2 = imported principal with literal PrincipalAccount equal (TokenComparison.SAME) to the literal endpoint stack account.
  Resource side when: identity side not written for an established same-account immutable role; service principal; or CallerPolicy = ExternallyManaged.
  Under Automatic, fail with InvalidOperationException (grantee, endpoint, reason, two remedies) for: imported principals with any unresolved account (ONE_ or BOTH_UNRESOLVED),
  different literal account, AccountPrincipal/ArnPrincipal. ExternallyManaged never writes identity policy and adds an Annotations info naming the required caller-side identity policy.
- WebFunctionEndpointConstruct.FromEndpointAttributes(scope, id, WebFunctionEndpointAttributes) → IWebFunctionEndpoint that owns nothing: identity grants for established (E1/E2) grantees only;
  any grant requiring the resource policy, ExternallyManaged grants, and GrantCloudFrontInvoke throw ("resource policy of an imported endpoint is externally owned").
  Parse endpoint name/account/region from a literal ARN; token ARN ⇒ unresolved account (only E1 grantees can be granted).

Tests (one per §10.2 table row + §15 IAM bullets): E1 role/Function/WebFunctionConstruct (incl. env-agnostic stacks) → identity statement on the specific endpoint ARN only, no ResourcePolicy;
E2 mutable → attached policy; E2 Mutable=false → resource statement only (imported endpoint throws); imported role with token ARN or env-agnostic stack under Automatic → throws AND no AWS::IAM::Policy synthesized;
same under ExternallyManaged → resource statement + annotation; different literal account Automatic throws / ExternallyManaged resource-only with no principal statements in returned Grant;
service principal → resource only; Account/ArnPrincipal Automatic throws / ExternallyManaged resource-only; ExternallyManaged with E1 → resource only; ApplicationManaged throws;
imported endpoint ExternallyManaged throws; regression test with a fake IResourceWithPolicy returning StatementAdded=false → GrantInvoke throws.
Golden template: cross-account ExternallyManaged grant + same-account grant.

Exclusions: WebFunctionOrigin, Testing helpers, docs. Do not change resource-policy ownership semantics from the previous bead.
Security: never synthesize an identity policy for a principal whose account is not established; never report partial cross-account configuration as complete.
acceptance_criteria:
- GrantInvoke implements §10.2 revision 3 exactly; no use of AddToPrincipalOrResource, Grant.Success, or AssertSuccess in the implementation (code review check).
- Every §10.2 table row has a passing test, including the "no AWS::IAM::Policy synthesized" check for unresolved imported roles and the StatementAdded=false regression.
- FromEndpointAttributes returns an endpoint with the documented limited capabilities and clear exceptions.
- ExternallyManaged emits the info annotation; Automatic failures name grantee, endpoint, reason, and remedies.
- Golden templates unchanged except the new one; validation gates pass.

title: T3a: Add AddEndpoint, single-owner resource policy, and GrantCloudFrontInvoke
description:
Purpose: multiple endpoints and the single-owner resource policy. Design §8.3 (AddEndpoint), §8.4, §10.3, §12.2–§12.3, §14, §15 (Resource-policy ownership).

Deliverables:
- WebFunctionConstruct.AddEndpoint(string id, IWebFunctionEndpointOptions): validates unique EndpointName per function (a second "default" is a duplicate → InvalidOperationException);
  every endpoint routes 100% to the current revision; returns WebFunctionEndpointConstruct; Endpoints list includes default + added.
- Single-owner resource policy (private to WebFunctionConstruct): lazily create one CfnResourcePolicy child "ResourcePolicy" (ResourceArn = function GetAtt FunctionArn,
  PolicyDocument = an iam.PolicyDocument) on first contribution; later contributions AddStatements to the same document. No resource when there are no statements.
  WebFunctionConstruct must NOT expose a public AddToResourcePolicy.
- WebFunctionEndpointConstruct implements IResourceWithPolicy: AddToResourcePolicy(statement) requires statement Resources to be exactly this endpoint's ARN (else ArgumentException) and forwards to the function's policy.
- GrantCloudFrontInvoke(string distributionArn): adds {Principal cloudfront.amazonaws.com, Action lambda:InvokeWebFunctionEndpoint, Resource endpoint ARN,
  Condition StringEquals aws:SourceArn = distributionArn}; accepts tokens or literals; throws for ApplicationManaged. Identical statements deduplicate (verify PolicyDocument behavior in a test).

Tests: no statements → no ResourcePolicy; many contributions → exactly one; multiple distributions/endpoints → all statements, each scoped to the correct endpoint ARN;
different contribution orders → equal statement sets; repeated grants → no duplicates; foreign Resource → throws; ApplicationManaged → throws;
multiple endpoints with different auth types synthesize correctly; duplicate endpoint names rejected; API-surface test that WebFunctionConstruct has no public AddToResourcePolicy.
Add a golden template: two endpoints (IamAuth + ApplicationManaged) with two explicit CloudFront grants.

Exclusions: GrantInvoke, imports (FromEndpointAttributes), WebFunctionOrigin, Testing helpers, docs.
Security: never emit wildcard endpoint resources (endpoint/*) or unscoped CloudFront principals.
acceptance_criteria:
- AddEndpoint works with unique-name validation; all endpoints weight 100 to the current revision.
- At most one AWS::Lambda::ResourcePolicy per function, created only when a statement exists; all contributions preserved; duplicates removed.
- Endpoint-scoped AddToResourcePolicy and GrantCloudFrontInvoke behave per §8.4/§10.3, including negatives.
- No public AddToResourcePolicy on WebFunctionConstruct.
- New golden template added; all existing goldens unchanged; validation gates pass.
notes:
T3a IMPLEMENTED (AddEndpoint + single-owner resource policy + endpoint AddToResourcePolicy + GrantCloudFrontInvoke). Not committed per task restriction.

DELIVERABLES:
- WebFunctionConstruct.AddEndpoint(string id, IWebFunctionEndpointOptions options): ArgumentNullException on null id/options; per-function EndpointName uniqueness via HashSet(StringComparer.Ordinal) seeded with the default endpoint's name -> duplicate (incl. a second 'default') throws InvalidOperationException; returns the endpoint created by the shared private CreateEndpoint (news WebFunctionEndpointConstruct, adds endpoint.CfnEndpoint.AddResourceDependency(revision), appends to the list). New public IReadOnlyList<WebFunctionEndpointConstruct> Endpoints reflects default + added endpoints, in creation order. Every endpoint routes RevisionWeights=[{current revision, 100}].
- Single-owner resource policy (private to WebFunctionConstruct, NO public AddToResourcePolicy): AddResourcePolicyStatement(statement) lazily creates ONE iam.PolicyDocument and ONE Amazon.CDK.AWS.Lambda.CfnResourcePolicy child id 'ResourcePolicy' (ResourceArn = Function GetAtt FunctionArn, PolicyDocument = the shared document). No statements => no AWS::Lambda::ResourcePolicy resource. Later contributions AddStatements to the same document; all preserved; identical statements deduplicate at PolicyDocument resolution (verified: 2 identical grants -> 1 statement).
- WebFunctionEndpointConstruct now : Resource, IResourceWithPolicyV2 and implements AddToResourcePolicy(statement): requires statement.Resources length == 1 and string-equals this endpoint's EndpointArn (ArgumentNullException on null; ArgumentException for foreign resource, another endpoint, the whole function, or wildcard) and forwards to the function policy; returns AddToResourcePolicyResult{StatementAdded=true, PolicyDependable=the policy}.
- GrantCloudFrontInvoke(string distributionArn): InvalidOperationException when AuthType != IamAuth (ApplicationManaged rejected); ArgumentNullException on null; literal ARNs validated (token-aware: unresolved tokens skipped); emits {Effect Allow, Principal Service cloudfront.amazonaws.com, Action lambda:InvokeWebFunctionEndpoint, Resource = endpoint ARN, Condition StringEquals aws:SourceArn = distributionArn} -> endpoint AddToResourcePolicy. Repeated equivalent grants deduplicate. Never creates/modifies a Distribution.

DEViation (mechanical, contract-identical; reported): the design named IResourceWithPolicy, but that interface is DEPRECATED in CDK 2.274 ('prefer IResourceWithPolicyV2'). Implemented the non-deprecated Amazon.CDK.AWS.IAM.IResourceWithPolicyV2 instead. Because its AddToResourcePolicy returns IAddToResourcePolicyResult (not the concrete AddToResourcePolicyResult), the public method keeps the concrete return type and the interface is satisfied by an explicit implementation that forwards to it. src build stays at 0 warnings.

NEW TESTS/GOLDEN: test/.../WebFunctionResourcePolicyTests.cs (19 tests: no-statements -> no policy; single grant -> one policy with correct ResourceArn/Principal/Action/Condition/Resource; two distributions -> 2 statements / 1 policy; repeated grant -> dedup to 1; order-independence; two endpoints -> 1 policy / 2 statements scoped to 2 distinct endpoint ARNs; ApplicationManaged -> throws; invalid literal ARNs (non-ARN, lambda function ARN, truncated cloudfront) -> ArgumentException; token ARN accepted; foreign/wildcard Resource -> ArgumentException; endpoint.EndpointArn accepted; duplicate endpoint names -> InvalidOperationException; Endpoints + per-endpoint weight-100 assertions; API-surface reflection proving WebFunctionConstruct has no public AddToResourcePolicy; IResourceWithPolicyV2 assignability). New golden web-function-multi-endpoint.json (two endpoints IamAuth + ApplicationManaged, two CloudFront grants -> exactly ONE AWS::Lambda::ResourcePolicy with two SourceArn-scoped statements). Infrastructure: WebFunctionValidation.ValidateCloudFrontDistributionArn added; regex ^arn:[a-z0-9-]+:cloudfront::[0-9]{12}:distribution/[A-Za-z0-9]+$.

RESULTS (JSII_SILENCE_WARNING_UNTESTED_NODE_VERSION=1, -c Release): src build 0 warnings/0 errors on net8.0/9.0/10.0/11.0; full solution suite 1464 passed / 0 failed / 0 skipped (366 x 4 TFMs; prior baseline 1384, +20 tests/TFM = 19 resource-policy + 1 golden); all 22 pre-existing golden templates UNCHANGED (only the new web-function-multi-endpoint.json added; 23 total). No existing construct modified. No new dependencies. Coverage: no local script; CI gate 80% (external devops template); changes additive and covered.

ACCEPTANCE: AddEndpoint unique-name validation + every endpoint weight 100; exactly one AWS::Lambda::ResourcePolicy per function created only when a statement exists, all contributions preserved, duplicates removed; endpoint-scoped AddToResourcePolicy and GrantCloudFrontInvoke per section 8.4/10.3 including negatives; no public AddToResourcePolicy on WebFunctionConstruct; new golden added, existing goldens unchanged; validation gates pass. T3b items (GrantInvoke, endpoint imports) intentionally NOT implemented.
close_reason: T3a complete: AddEndpoint with per-function endpoint-name uniqueness (duplicate incl. second default rejected); Endpoints collection; single lazily-created AWS::Lambda::ResourcePolicy per function (no resource when no statements, all contributions preserved, identical statements deduplicated via PolicyDocument); endpoint-scoped IResourceWithPolicyV2.AddToResourcePolicy (foreign/wildcard resource rejected); GrantCloudFrontInvoke (cloudfront.amazonaws.com, lambda:InvokeWebFunctionEndpoint, StringEquals aws:SourceArn, endpoint-only resource, token-aware ARN validation, ApplicationManaged rejected, dedup). One reported mechanical deviation: IResourceWithPolicy is deprecated in CDK 2.274 -> implemented IResourceWithPolicyV2 with an explicit interface forwarder. Build 0 warnings/0 errors; full suite 1464/1464 passed across net8.0/9.0/10.0/11.0 (+20 tests/TFM); 22 existing goldens unchanged + 1 new multi-endpoint golden. No existing construct modified.

title: T2: Implement core WebFunctionConstruct (function, revision, default endpoint, role, logs, code bucket)
description:
Purpose: the core L3 construct that owns one Web Function lifecycle. Design §7, §8.2 (bucket statement), §8.3, §12.1, §12.2, §12.4, §14, §15 (Synthesis/template, Code bucket).

Deliverables:
- WebFunctionConstruct : Construct, IGrantable (src/LayeredCraft.Cdk.Constructs/WebFunctionConstruct.cs) creating, with these STABLE child IDs:
  "Function" (CfnWebFunction; set Node.DefaultChild), "Revision" (CfnWebFunctionRevision), "DefaultEndpoint" (WebFunctionEndpointConstruct whose L1 child is "Resource"),
  "ExecutionRole" (only when props.Role is null; AWSLambdaBasicExecutionRole), "LogGroup" (only for WebFunctionLogs.Create; name /aws/lambda/web/{FunctionName}).
- Pass the LITERAL FunctionName (not Ref/ARN) to Revision.FunctionName and Endpoint.FunctionName; add explicit AddResourceDependency function←revision←endpoint (§8.3 notes, §12.4).
- Revision: S3Object {Bucket, Key, VersionId?}; RuntimeConfig.Runtime; ServiceConfig {ExecutionRoleArn, EnvironmentVariables (+ AWS_LAMBDA_NODEJS_ENTRYPOINT from EntryPoint),
  TimeoutSeconds, MaxConcurrencyPerEnvironment, TelemetryConfig.LoggingConfig {LogGroup (Create/Use only), ApplicationLogLevel, SystemLogLevel}}; Description. No KmsKeyArn.
- WebFunctionLogs.Use(group): pass name; logGroup.GrantWrite(role) only when the name is outside /aws/lambda/*.
- WebFunctionEndpointConstruct (src/.../WebFunctionEndpointConstruct.cs): Amazon.CDK.Resource subclass, internal ctor, exposes EndpointName, EndpointArn, DomainName,
  Url ("https://"+DomainName), AuthType, EndpointType, Regions, WebFunction. Endpoint L1: AuthType, EndpointName, EndpointType, Regions, RevisionWeights=[{current revision, 100}],
  ScalingConfig/ThrottleConfig only when set, Description. (Grants/policy/AddEndpoint come in later beads; do not stub public members that later beads own unless needed to compile.)
- Code binding: WebFunctionCode.FromBucket.Bind implementation:
  * Automatic: add the least-privilege statement from §8.2 (lambda.amazonaws.com, s3:GetObject+s3:GetObjectVersion on the object ARN, StringEquals aws:SourceAccount,
    ArnLike aws:SourceArn arn:{partition}:lambda:{region}:{account}:web-function/{FunctionName}/revision/* using the FUNCTION stack's account/region);
    fail (InvalidOperationException) if AddToResourcePolicy returns StatementAdded=false; add revision dependency on the policy dependable.
  * Owned Bucket L2 created in the app: fail if versioning is not enabled or encryption is KMS_MANAGED/DSSE_MANAGED (inspect the owned bucket's CfnBucket; imported buckets are not inspected).
  * Owned bucket in another stack while the function stack's account/region is unresolved → fail.
  * ExternallyManaged: add nothing.
- Golden templates (using the T0 harness) for: single IamAuth function with defaults; ApplicationManaged with ServiceDefault logs; Use(logGroup) + supplied role; Automatic owned bucket; ExternallyManaged imported bucket.

Tests (§15): template assertions for every property above, defaults, DependsOn chain, literal FunctionName on all three, no KmsKeyArn, log group variants, role variants, code-bucket matrix, and §14 construct-level negatives.
Exclusions: AddEndpoint, resource policy, GrantInvoke, GrantCloudFrontInvoke, imports, CloudFront, Testing namespace helpers, docs. No changes to existing constructs.
Security: never grant s3 read beyond the single object key and the /revision/* SourceArn pattern.
acceptance_criteria:
- Child IDs exactly Function, Revision, DefaultEndpoint(/Resource), ExecutionRole, LogGroup; Node.DefaultChild is the CfnWebFunction.
- Revision and endpoint receive the literal FunctionName and explicit DependsOn edges (asserted).
- Default log group /aws/lambda/web/{name}, 14 days, Delete; ServiceDefault creates none and omits LoggingConfig.LogGroup; Use() creates none.
- Code-bucket Automatic/ExternallyManaged/owned-validation/cross-stack matrix implemented and tested, statement matches §8.2 exactly.
- WebFunctionConstruct.GrantPrincipal is the execution role (e.g. table.GrantReadData(webFunction) works; tested).
- New golden templates added; existing golden templates unchanged.
- Validation gates pass.
notes:
T2 IMPLEMENTED (core WebFunctionConstruct). Not committed per task restriction.

DELIVERABLES:
- src/.../WebFunctionConstruct.cs (NEW): public sealed class WebFunctionConstruct : Construct, IGrantable. Validates FunctionName/Timeout/MaxConcurrencyPerEnvironment/EnvironmentVariables/EntryPoint via WebFunctionValidation; creates stable children Function (CfnWebFunction, Node.DefaultChild), Revision (CfnWebFunctionRevision), DefaultEndpoint (WebFunctionEndpointConstruct), ExecutionRole (only when props.Role is null; AWSLambdaBasicExecutionRole), LogGroup (only for WebFunctionLogs.Create). Public: FunctionName, FunctionArn, RevisionId, RevisionArn, Role, GrantPrincipal (=Role.GrantPrincipal), LogGroup (null for ServiceDefault), DefaultEndpoint. Revision ServiceConfig carries ExecutionRoleArn, EnvironmentVariables (+ AWS_LAMBDA_NODEJS_ENTRYPOINT from EntryPoint), TimeoutSeconds, MaxConcurrencyPerEnvironment, TelemetryConfig.LoggingConfig{LogGroup,ApplicationLogLevel,SystemLogLevel}; no KmsKeyArn. FunctionName passed LITERAL to Revision and Endpoint. Explicit deps: Revision.AddResourceDependency(Function); Revision.Node.AddDependency(Role/created LogGroup/bucket PolicyDependable); endpoint.AddResourceDependency(Revision).
- src/.../WebFunctionEndpointConstruct.cs (NEW): public sealed class WebFunctionEndpointConstruct : Resource; internal ctor (scope,id,webFunction,options); validates EndpointName/Regions(homeRegion=Stack.Of(function).Region)/MaxEnvironments/RateLimit; creates the L1 child id 'Resource' (CfnWebFunctionEndpoint) and sets Node.DefaultChild; exposes WebFunction, EndpointName, AuthType, EndpointType, Regions, EndpointArn, DomainName, Url. ScalingConfig/ThrottleConfig emitted only when set; RevisionWeights=[{current RevisionId, 100}].
- src/.../Models/WebFunctionCode.cs (MODIFIED, T2-owned completion): added internal abstract WebFunctionCodeConfig Bind(WebFunctionConstruct) on WebFunctionCode + override in WebFunctionCodeFromBucket; automatic bucket policy per design §8.2 EXACTLY (lambda.amazonaws.com; s3:GetObject,s3:GetObjectVersion; Resource arn:{partition}:s3:::{bucket}/{key}; StringEquals aws:SourceAccount; ArnLike aws:SourceArn arn:{partition}:lambda:{region}:{account}:web-function/{FunctionName}/revision/*; partition/account/region from the FUNCTION stack); StatementAdded=false -> InvalidOperationException; ExternallyManaged -> no statement; owned bucket validated (versioning required; AWS-managed KMS aws/s3 or DSSE rejected), imported buckets not inspected; owned bucket in another stack while function stack account/Region unresolved -> InvalidOperationException; revision depends on result.PolicyDependable.
- src/.../Models/WebFunctionCodeConfig.cs (NEW): internal sealed config {Bucket,Key,VersionId,PolicyDependable}.

FILES: src: WebFunctionConstruct.cs, WebFunctionEndpointConstruct.cs, Models/WebFunctionCode.cs (mod), Models/WebFunctionCodeConfig.cs; tests: WebFunctionConstructTests.cs (45 cases), WebFunctionConstructGoldenTemplateTests.cs (5 goldens); GoldenTemplates: web-function-default / -application-managed / -use-log-group / -owned-bucket / -externally-managed .json. No existing construct changed. No new dependencies.

IMPLEMENTATION FINDING (not a public API deviation): the S3 Bucket L2 sets VersioningConfiguration/BucketEncryption from JavaScript, so the CLR getters expose a JSII AnonymousObject and typed casts to CfnBucket.*Property return null. Owned-bucket inspection therefore reads the values via Stack.Of(bucket).Resolve(...) (plain camelCase dictionaries: 'status', 'serverSideEncryptionConfiguration'[].'serverSideEncryptionByDefault'.'sseAlgorithm'/'kmsMasterKeyId'). Verified empirically: Versioned=true -> {'status':'Enabled'}; KMS_MANAGED -> {'sseAlgorithm':'aws:kms'} (no key) -> rejected; DSSE_MANAGED -> {'sseAlgorithm':'aws:kms:dsse'} -> rejected; default S3-managed bucket emits no BucketEncryption -> allowed.

§18 OPEN QUESTION 5 RESULT: ScalingConfig/ThrottleConfig are emitted only when MaxEnvironments/RateLimit are set (asserted by Construct_ShouldOmitScalingAndThrottleWhenUnset). CloudFormation update semantics are 'omit = keep existing value', so removing these values after a deployment would NOT clear them via omission; clearing would require explicitly sending an empty object. Whether CloudFormation accepts an empty ScalingConfig/ThrottleConfig sub-object is NOT verified (no deploy performed; deploy verification is deferred to T7 per design). Recommendation: document the clear-via-explicit-empty-object requirement and confirm in the T7 sandbox.

TESTS/RESULTS (JSII_SILENCE_WARNING_UNTESTED_NODE_VERSION=1, -c Release):
- dotnet build LayeredCraft.Cdk.Constructs.slnx -c Release -> Build succeeded, 0 warnings, 0 errors.
- New behavior suite: 45 tests pass (construct/revision/default endpoint, stable logical ids, literal FunctionName on all three, DependsOn chain, runtime nodejs24.x, S3Object with/without VersionId, env vars incl AWS_LAMBDA_NODEJS_ENTRYPOINT, timeout/concurrency/no KmsKeyArn, default+supplied role, three logging modes + GrantWrite only outside /aws/lambda/*, endpoint name/type/Regions/AuthType/scaling/throttle present-absent/revision-weight-100, GrantPrincipal=dynamodb:GetItem via table.GrantReadData, bucket matrix incl. imported+Automatic throw, ExternallyManaged no-policy, unversioned/KMS_MANAGED/cross-stack throws, token FunctionName allowed, all §14 construct negatives).
- Golden suite: 22/22 pass with ZERO diff (17 pre-existing UNCHANGED + 5 new Web Function goldens).
- Full solution: dotnet test --solution LayeredCraft.Cdk.Constructs.slnx -c Release -> 1384 passed / 0 failed / 0 skipped (346 x net8.0/net9.0/net10.0/net11.0); prior baseline 1184; +50 tests/TFM.
- Coverage: no local script; CI gate 80% (external devops template); src changes are additive and covered by the new tests.

ACCEPTANCE: all child IDs stable; DefaultChild=CfnWebFunction; literal FunctionName + DependsOn asserted; logging modes asserted; bucket-policy matrix implemented + tested; GrantPrincipal is the execution role; new goldens added, existing unchanged; no existing construct modified.
close_reason: T2 complete: core WebFunctionConstruct (Function/Revision/DefaultEndpoint/ExecutionRole/LogGroup with stable ids), WebFunctionEndpointConstruct (L1 child 'Resource', Node.DefaultChild, revision weight 100, scaling/throttle only when set), and the WebFunctionCode.Bind artifact seam (automatic/external bucket policy per §8.2, versioning + AWS-managed-KMS rejection on owned buckets, cross-stack unresolved-env failure, revision depends on PolicyDependable). Literal FunctionName + explicit DependsOn chain; no revision KMS. Build 0 warnings/0 errors; full suite 1384/1384 passed across net8.0/9.0/10.0/11.0 (+50 tests/TFM); 22/22 golden tests zero-diff (17 existing unchanged + 5 new). GrantPrincipal is the execution role. No existing construct modified. §18 Q5: omit=keep confirmed by design of our output; clearing needs explicit empty objects, deploy verification deferred to T7.

title: T1: Add Web Function public models, options, and value validation
description:
Purpose: introduce the public model/value types every later bead consumes, with value validation. Design §8.1, §8.2, §8.3 (props + WebFunctionLogs), §8.4 (options/attributes), §8.5 (origin props), §8.7, §10.2 (WebFunctionCallerPolicy, WebFunctionInvokeGrantOptions), §14.

Deliverables (namespace LayeredCraft.Cdk.Constructs.Models unless noted; follow the newest Cognito style: get-only interfaces + init-only sealed records, XML docs):
- Enums: WebFunctionAuthType {IamAuth, ApplicationManaged}; WebFunctionEndpointType {HomeRegion, MultiRegion, PerRegion};
  WebFunctionCodeBucketPolicy {Automatic, ExternallyManaged}; WebFunctionOriginPermissions {Automatic, ExternallyManaged};
  WebFunctionCallerPolicy {Automatic, ExternallyManaged}.
- WebFunctionRuntime (sealed; NodeJs24X = "nodejs24.x"; Of(string)).
- WebFunctionCode (abstract, private protected ctor, closed hierarchy) with static FromBucket(IBucket, string key, WebFunctionCodeFromBucketOptions?)
  and WebFunctionCodeFromBucketOptions {ObjectVersion, BucketPolicy = Automatic}. The internal Bind contract to the construct is
  declared but bucket-policy wiring is implemented in the core-construct bead; keep the binding surface internal so FromAsset can be added later.
- WebFunctionLogs (abstract, closed): Create(RetentionDays? retention = null [→ TWO_WEEKS], RemovalPolicy? [→ DESTROY]), Use(ILogGroup), ServiceDefault().
- IWebFunctionConstructProps / WebFunctionConstructProps exactly per §8.3 (FunctionName, Code, Endpoint required; Runtime, EntryPoint,
  EnvironmentVariables, Timeout=30s, MaxConcurrencyPerEnvironment, Description, Role, Logs=Create(), ApplicationLogLevel, SystemLogLevel
  reusing Amazon.CDK.AWS.Lambda enums). NO EncryptionKey property.
- IWebFunctionEndpointOptions / WebFunctionEndpointOptions (EndpointName="default", required AuthType, EndpointType=HomeRegion, Regions, MaxEnvironments, RateLimit, Description).
- WebFunctionEndpointAttributes (EndpointArn, DomainName, AuthType required; EndpointType=HomeRegion).
- WebFunctionInvokeGrantOptions {CallerPolicy = Automatic}.
- WebFunctionOriginProps (explicit members only: OriginId, OriginPath, CustomHeaders, ConnectionAttempts, ConnectionTimeout, ReadTimeout,
  KeepaliveTimeout, ResponseCompletionTimeout, OriginShieldEnabled, OriginShieldRegion) and sealed WebFunctionOriginWithOacProps : WebFunctionOriginProps
  {OriginAccessControl, Permissions = Automatic}. Must NOT expose ProtocolPolicy or OriginAccessControlId.
- Internal validation helpers (local to new types; do not refactor shared code or existing constructs) for §14 value rules: FunctionName
  regex 1–64; EndpointName 1–64 [A-Za-z0-9_-]; Timeout 3–900 whole seconds; MaxConcurrencyPerEnvironment 1–128; MaxEnvironments 2–10000;
  RateLimit grid {0} ∪ 100..1000 step 100 ∪ 2000..10000 step 1000; Regions rules; env var key regex; EntryPoint relative/no "..";
  reserved AWS_LAMBDA_HTTP_ENDPOINT; EntryPoint vs AWS_LAMBDA_NODEJS_ENTRYPOINT conflict. Unresolved tokens (Token.IsUnresolved) are skipped, never rejected.
  Exception types per §14 (ArgumentException / ArgumentOutOfRangeException / InvalidOperationException).

Expected files: src/LayeredCraft.Cdk.Constructs/Models/WebFunction*.cs (one type per file or small cohesive groups); test/.../WebFunctionModelsTests.cs (+ validation tests).
Exclusions: no constructs, no CloudFormation resources, no IBucket policy mutation yet, no testing-namespace helpers, no docs.
Edge cases: FunctionName must allow tokens; nullable reference types enabled; records must be init-only (no Action<> mutation APIs anywhere).

- WebFunctionConstructProps cannot be constructed without FunctionName, Code, and Endpoint; WebFunctionEndpointOptions cannot be constructed without AuthType (compile-time `required`).

- WebFunctionLogs.Create() defaults are TWO_WEEKS and DESTROY (tested).

- Validation gates pass.

title: AWS Lambda Web Functions support — LayeredCraft.Cdk.Constructs
description:
Implement AWS Lambda Web Functions support in LayeredCraft.Cdk.Constructs per the APPROVED design (revision 3):
docs/designs/lambda-web-functions-integration.md (authoritative; GitHub issue #98).

Scope: new additive constructs WebFunctionConstruct, WebFunctionEndpointConstruct/IWebFunctionEndpoint, WebFunctionOrigin,
WebFunctionCode.FromBucket, WebFunctionLogs, supporting models, Testing helpers, docs, and a mandatory AWS sandbox release gate.

Non-negotiable constraints (design §2, §6, §8, §10.2, §12.4):
- Hybrid composition; L3 over CDK L1 (CfnWebFunction/Revision/Endpoint, CfnResourcePolicy); no upstream alpha/L2 dependency;
  upstream L2 types never appear in the public API.
- Existing constructs (LambdaFunctionConstruct, StaticSiteConstruct, DynamoDbTableConstruct, CognitoUserPoolConstruct) are
  NOT modified; their synthesized templates must not change (golden templates from cdkc T0).
- Explicit AuthType on every endpoint (no default). Single-owner resource policy per function. Same-stack automatic OAC
  permissions only. Limited endpoint imports (no whole-function import). Existing S3 artifacts only (no FromAsset).
  Default log retention TWO_WEEKS. No customer-managed revision KMS key. Workload-neutral (Next.js, ASP.NET Core shim,
  Blazor Static SSR) with no workload-specific constructs.
- GrantInvoke follows the revision-3 algorithm in §10.2 (account establishment E1/E2, Automatic vs ExternallyManaged).
  Never use Grant.AddToPrincipalOrResource or trust Grant.Success/AssertSuccess.
- Amazon.CDK.Lib floor 2.274.0.

Rules for every implementation agent:
- Implement only the claimed bead's scope. If the design is ambiguous or seems wrong, stop and record a blocker note on
  the bead (bd update <id> --append-notes ...) instead of changing the design.
- Do not commit, push, open PRs, publish NuGet packages, or close GitHub issue #98 unless separately authorized by the maintainer.
- Do not deploy to AWS except in the sandbox bead, and only with maintainer-provided non-production credentials.
- Do not modify the Sharedale repository.
- Validation gates (run from repo root): `dotnet restore LayeredCraft.Cdk.Constructs.slnx`, `dotnet build LayeredCraft.Cdk.Constructs.slnx -c Release`,
  `dotnet test --solution LayeredCraft.Cdk.Constructs.slnx -c Release` (Microsoft.Testing.Platform, see global.json); CI requires
  80% coverage across net8.0–net11.0. Docs: `uv run mkdocs build --clean`. If Node >24 prints jsii warnings, set
  JSII_SILENCE_WARNING_UNTESTED_NODE_VERSION=1.
- Test conventions: xUnit v3, AwesomeAssertions, AutoFixture TestKit customizations, `[Collection("CDK Tests")]`, Template.FromStack
  after constructs are added (see CLAUDE.md "Testing Patterns").
- Close a bead only when its acceptance criteria are met; record validation evidence (commands run + results) in notes.

Feature completion is gated by the "Verify release acceptance criteria" bead, which depends on the sandbox deployment bead.
Optional bead T4a never blocks completion.
acceptance_criteria: All required child beads closed, including the AWS sandbox release gate and the release acceptance verification bead; optional spike may be open or closed.

title: T7b: Create sandbox CDK app and deploy/smoke/destroy scripts (no deployment)
description:
Purpose: sandbox CDK app and smoke-test tooling that exercises the implemented constructs exactly as a consumer would. No deployment in this bead. Design §19.1 item 3 (all sub-items), §9, §12.

Deliverables under samples/web-functions/sandbox/ (not in the library slnx/CI):
- A CDK app (C#) referencing the library project, with explicit Env (account/region from context or env vars; never hard-coded production values):
  * ArtifactsStack: owned versioned SSE-S3 Bucket used with WebFunctionCodeBucketPolicy.Automatic (bucket stack deployed and artifacts uploaded BEFORE the app stack, because the
    object must exist before the revision is created and Automatic adds the statement to the bucket's own stack).
  * A pre-provisioned "external" bucket (created by the script or a separate stack with its own lambda.amazonaws.com read policy) imported via Bucket.FromBucketName and used with ExternallyManaged.
  * AppStack: Next.js Web Function (IamAuth) behind a Distribution via WebFunctionOrigin.WithOriginAccessControl (default uncached + ALL_VIEWER_EXCEPT_HOST_HEADER, /_next/static/* cached);
    ASP.NET Core Web Function (IamAuth) with a second endpoint (for the endpoint-specific denial test) and GrantInvoke to a dedicated "caller" IAM role assumable by the operator;
    Blazor Web Function (IamAuth) behind OAC (fingerprinted/static assets cached); context flags to (a) switch artifacts to the v2 build (revision update), (b) add/remove a second
    distribution on the Next.js endpoint (resource-policy lifecycle), (c) optionally add an ExternallyManaged cross-account grant for a second sandbox account.
  * Outputs needed by the smoke script (endpoint URLs/ARNs, distribution domains/ids, caller role ARN). Use the library's naming; prefix all names with a sandbox prefix.
- smoke.sh (bash, AWS CLI v2 + curl with --aws-sigv4 "aws:amz:<region>:lambda" and header x-amz-content-sha256: UNSIGNED-PAYLOAD) implementing every §19.1 3.x check with expected status codes,
  `aws lambda-web get-resource-policy` inspection, revision/endpoint state checks, and a machine-readable summary; deploy.sh (ordered: artifacts stack → upload zips → app stack) and destroy.sh
  (destroys stacks, empties/deletes buckets incl. all object versions, deletes log groups).
- README.md: prerequisites, required IAM permissions, non-production account requirement, cost notes, step-by-step run, cleanup, and how to record evidence.

Validation in this bead: `cdk synth` of the sandbox app succeeds locally without deploying (use dummy account/region context); scripts pass shellcheck if available. No AWS deployment.
Exclusions: running against AWS (next bead); changes to library production code (record blockers instead).

- Sandbox CDK app synthesizes using only the public library API and covers every §19.1 item 3 scenario via stacks/context flags.

- No deployment performed; library validation gates still pass.

title: T7a: Create sandbox workload sample apps (Next.js, ASP.NET Core shim, Blazor Static SSR) and artifact builds
description:
Purpose: minimal, deployable workload artifacts for the sandbox release gate. Independent of the library code; can start immediately. Design §16 recipes, §19.1 items 2–3.8.

Deliverables under samples/web-functions/apps/ (consumer-style sample code, NOT library code; must not be added to LayeredCraft.Cdk.Constructs.slnx or the PR CI build):
1. nextjs/: minimal Next.js app (one server-rendered page that prints a request-time value + one static asset), `output: "standalone"`, and an index.js entry that sets
   HOSTNAME/PORT from AWS_LAMBDA_HTTP_ENDPOINT ("host:port"), handles SIGTERM with exit(0), then require("./server.js"). Zip layout: standalone output + .next/static + public at zip root.
2. aspnetcore/: minimal ASP.NET Core API (GET /status returning JSON incl. a build id; one protected-by-IAM-only route is fine) published self-contained linux-arm64 as apphost `server`;
   zip root contains index.js = `process.execve("/var/task/server", ["/var/task/server"], process.env);` and the publish output. App listens on http://$AWS_LAMBDA_HTTP_ENDPOINT,
   then POSTs `{}` to http://$AWS_LAMBDA_RUNTIME_API/2025-09-01/ready after StartAsync (skip when the variable is absent); no UseHttpsRedirection/HSTS; invariant globalization
   or app-local ICU (runtime has no libicu).
3. blazor/: minimal Blazor Static SSR app (one SSR page; wwwroot/app.css), same shim/readiness contract, untrimmed publish, ContentRootPath = AppContext.BaseDirectory

Constraints: samples get their own Directory.Build.props/Directory.Packages.props overrides if needed so they do not alter the library build; framework-only dependencies for .NET samples

title: T6a: Write Web Function construct docs, security guidance, and workload recipes
description:
Purpose: user documentation for the constructs and the three workload recipes. Design §16 (AUTHORITATIVE content list), §5 (facts), §10–§12 (security/deployment), §14 (documented-not-validated list), §8.7.

Deliverables:
- docs/constructs/web-function.md: overview; auth modes and who can reach an endpoint (ApplicationManaged is public even behind CloudFront; IamAuth ≠ user auth);
  WebFunctionCode.FromBucket requirements (versioning, s3:GetObject/GetObjectVersion, /revision/* SourceArn statement, optional VersionId semantics, cross-account buckets,
  SSE-KMS key policy, CDK bootstrap bucket incompatibility, object must exist before deploy); WebFunctionLogs (TWO_WEEKS default, ONE_MONTH example, ServiceDefault no expiry);
  endpoints/AddEndpoint and revision-change behavior; GrantInvoke table from §10.2 incl. ExternallyManaged contract and caller-side SigV4 (service lambda, UNSIGNED-PAYLOAD,
  Authorization stripping); single-owner resource-policy contract; WebFunctionOrigin (OAC, same-stack rule, ExternallyManaged, imported endpoints);
  cache/header guidance (§11.3: never forward Host / use ALL_VIEWER_EXCEPT_HOST_HEADER, Authorization in cache policy, Lambda@Edge origin triggers rejected, opt-in Regions 403);
  replacement table (§12.2); validation errors (§14); KMS deferral + unsupported escape hatch (§8.7); limitations.
- Workload recipes (same page or docs/examples/web-functions.md): Next.js standalone; ASP.NET Core via Node.js execve shim (self-contained linux-arm64 apphost "server", index.js
  `process.execve("/var/task/server", ["/var/task/server"], process.env);`, Kestrel on http://$AWS_LAMBDA_HTTP_ENDPOINT, readiness POST to
  http://$AWS_LAMBDA_RUNTIME_API/2025-09-01/ready after start, app-local ICU or invariant globalization, no HTTPS redirection/HSTS); Blazor Static SSR (same shim; untrimmed server;
  ContentRootPath = AppContext.BaseDirectory when AWS_LAMBDA_HTTP_ENDPOINT is set; wwwroot/_framework shipped; cache fingerprinted assets; Interactive Server/Auto/legacy Blazor Server
  UNSUPPORTED — WebSockets rejected). Mark execve/readiness as not documented by AWS. Reference https://github.com/j-d-ha/lambda-web-function-not-node.
- mkdocs.yml nav entry under Constructs (and examples page if created). Do NOT add the design doc to nav.
- docs/examples/index.md: §9 examples.

Exclusions: README/CHANGELOG/testing docs (separate bead); no code changes.
Validation: `uv run mkdocs build --clean` succeeds; every code sample matches the implemented public API (cross-check against src/).
acceptance_criteria:
- docs/constructs/web-function.md and recipes cover every §16 item, including security callouts and the §10.2 grant table.
- Three workload recipes are complete and explicitly distinguish Blazor Static SSR from Interactive Server.
- mkdocs nav updated; mkdocs build succeeds; samples match the real API.
notes: Also document (derived from design §8.2 + §12.1, found during planning): with WebFunctionCodeBucketPolicy.Automatic the code object must exist before the revision is created, so in practice the owned bucket must live in a separately deployed stack (deploy bucket stack -> upload artifact -> deploy function stack). A bucket created in the same stack as the function cannot be pre-populated.

title: T4a (optional): Spike narrow warning for managed AllViewer policy on Web Function origins
description:
OPTIONAL, time-boxed (≤ 4 hours). The feature must not depend on the outcome. Design §11.1 ("Removed in revision 2" paragraph), §18 item 4, §19 T4a.

Question: can a narrow, warning-only check detect a Distribution behavior that targets a WebFunctionOrigin with the MANAGED AllViewer origin request policy
(id 216adef6-5c7f-47e4-b989-5492eafa07d3) using only public CDK APIs on objects the library already holds (e.g. the BehaviorOptions/Origin object identity), WITHOUT resolving
CloudFormation templates, tokens, or CfnDistribution.DistributionConfig?

Rules: disposable spike code first (scratch or a throwaway test); no template-resolution machinery; zero false positives; emits Annotations warning only (never an error).
Outcome A (feasible and simple): implement it within WebFunctionOrigin with tests (warning present for AllViewer; absent for ALL_VIEWER_EXCEPT_HOST_HEADER and custom policies).
Outcome B (not feasible): record findings in notes and close as "won't implement"; documentation (cdkc docs bead) already covers the Host-header rule.
Exclusions: Lambda@Edge detection, opt-in Region detection, any IValidation that resolves templates.
acceptance_criteria:
- Findings recorded in notes with the exact approach tried and the decision (A or B).
- If A: warning-only check, tests prove no false positives, golden templates unchanged, validation gates pass.
- If B: no production code changes remain.
